# Driveline and wheel bearing noises (continued)

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Check front differential fluid level, inspect brake calipers and hubs, look at the rotor dust shield, and check U-joints and CV axles. [t495]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Check the front differential fluid level, drain it to inspect condition.
2. Inspect brake calipers and hubs for potential noise sources.

_Procedure reported by [t495]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Look closely at the dust shield on the back side of the rotor; a dented or loose shield can cause intermittent noise. [t495]
- [Partial] Check universal joints (U-joints) and CV axles, as these are common culprits after ruling out bearings. [t495]
